text:
elaine: Heads-up, we're getting a support escalation from BrightCart — sustained 429s + spikes in latency on their dedicated pool since ~02:00 UTC. They report auth failures intermittently as well. Can someone take?
support-lead: assigning to @omar oncall. Can you grab logs and prometheus graphs? Customer is on Dedicated eu-west-prod pool-42.
omar: I have the initial metrics — autoscaler shows repeated scale-up then immediate scale-down over last 40m. Pod count flies 2 -> 8 -> 3 -> 7. CPU/GPU utilization oscillating. Linking charts: https://grafana/redwood/d/abcd (sent)
ravi: seeing correlated 429 spikes at ~02:18, 02:32, 02:46. Errors: "quota_exceeded" in gateway logs but request rates are steady per-customer. Looks like per-instance throttles when capacity drops mid-burst.
elainE: (typo) sorry meant elaine: also customer says some clients get 401s around same time. Any chance token service retries clogged the control plane?
omar: checked auth-service logs — no elevated errors. 401s are from edge rejecting because of malformed header on retry floods from SDK. But that doesn't explain capacity churn.
lucy: I pulled autoscaler logs. Cooldown window is 60s, scaleDownStabilization 30s. But scaleDown is triggered on ephemeral metric that spikes low for ~40s because of our prefix cache warmup eviction. Looks like a warmup+kv-cache eviction pattern causing utilization dips -> scale down.
ravi: repro: run 20 concurrent requests with long tail tokens, then cancel half. KV cache gets partially populated, next traffic hits cache-miss -> short CPU spike then very low GPU usage due to blocking IO, autoscaler misinterprets.
omar: also noticed noisy neighbor tenant (tenant-371) had a batch job starting at 02:15 that briefly saturated NVMe and host IO — that amplified the eviction pattern.
sre-bot: alert: dedicated-pool-42 autoscaler flapping detected (5 cycles in 35m). Suggested action: increase scaleDownCooldown to 300s.
support-lead: customer impact: 429s and latency spikes for some endpoints; billing unaffected but heavy retries might produce extra cost. Customer asked for mitigation now.
elainE: (fixing name) elaine: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) increase scaleDown cooldown to 5m, 2) temporary pin pool to min=6 instances to absorb churn, 3) throttle tenant-371 batch job if possible, 4) rollout smoothing to autoscaler. Thoughts?
omar: I can push cooldown change to staging then prod. But pinning min capacity needs exec approval due to cost.
ravi: we can also adjust metric used for scaleDown to use 5m moving avg of request throughput instead of instantaneous host utilization. That would reduce sensitivity.
lucy: +1 on moving avg. Also add a short suppression window after scale-up to avoid immediate downscale on transient IO blips.
sre-bot: action: created incident runbook item #INC-2026 with steps to change cooldown and pin capacity.
omar: quick workaround applied: scaleDownCooldown patched to 180s on a test shard and min_instances bumped to 5 for pool-42 test group. Monitoring now.
(5m pass) ravi: after patch we see far fewer downscales. 429s dropped to baseline, latency stable. Tenant-371 batch throttled by infra team; removing noisy neighbor reduced NVMe pressure.
elainE: thanks team. Next steps: 1) propose permanent autoscaler tuning (scaleDownCooldown=300s, use 5m moving avg metric, suppression window 120s after scale-up), 2) add eviction telemetry to correlate KV-cache misses with scaling events, 3) docs for customers to avoid heavy background batch jobs on shared pools or request dedicated reservation.
support-lead: I'll send customer update summarizing corrective actions and ETA for permanent changes.
omar: I'll open a PR with the autoscaler defaults and link to telemetry dashboard.
lucy: I'll add a Grafana panel that overlays KV-cache evictions + autoscaler actions for easier triage.
sre-bot: incident resolved: mitigations in place, monitoring green for 25m. Marking as resolved unless regressions.
elainE: marking follow-up items for post-mortem and backlog grooming. Great work, team :tada:
